_comment: PROPOSAL, not implemented. P2P Stage 1. The snapshot: what one member's press of the
sync button produces, and what every other device stores.
Ledger decisions it encodes (2026-09-04):
- sync is a member's deliberate act, not a watcher: one press = one NAMED snapshot
- what travels is derived output (sheet packages, meta, quantities, reports), never
the source file, and in program-readable form - PDF is how it LOOKS, not how it
travels
- one writer per unit: the output's writer is the source's owner bot. So there is no
merge, only replace-by-owner-version; union across writers
- the snapshot is one self-describing, signed, encrypted blob - independent of how
it travels (LAN, reachable core, USB stick, e-mail, someone's cloud drive)
- received snapshots are forwarded on (gossip), so the founder's device need not be
on; 'everyone off' = everyone pending

_extension: Same container family as the succession package (PROJECT-PACKAGE-SUCCESSION §1),
distinguished by `kind`. A package moves a whole project between a person's devices;
a snapshot moves one writer's units between members. Same zip, same signing, same
encryption; different kind, different rules on receipt. One reader, two kinds - not
layout: ring.json            escrow ring as of this snapshot, CLEAR, owner-signed (fallback copy)
payload.bin          AES-256-GCM under the project key of `keyVersion`
signature.bin        ECDSA P-256 by the writer over sha256(snapshot.json) || sha256(payload.bin)
_clearManifest: The manifest is not encrypted, deliberately: a device must be able to answer 'do I
want this, do I already have it, may this writer write these units' BEFORE it has the
key - e.g. a file-carrier drop from a project it is not a member of. The manifest
names codes, counts and hashes; it names no content. Same boundary as the server's:

manifest._formatVersion: Readers accept N and N-1. Not advice - the fingerprint migration (0.001.53-55) is why.
manifest.writerPublicKey: <ECDSA P-256 SubjectPublicKeyInfo, base64 - so a receiver can verify before it has the ring>
_snapshotNumber: Per WRITER, monotonic, never reused. (writerBotCode, snapshotNumber) is the snapshot's
identity everywhere. A receiver that holds 17 discards a second 17; one that holds 16
and receives 18 stores 18 and marks 17 as missing - it may still arrive by another
route. Numbers, not clocks: device clocks are not trusted for ordering.
manifest._createdAtUtc: Display only. Never used to order or to resolve anything.
manifest.label: Барилга-А, 1-р давхрын шинэчлэл
manifest._label: What the member typed when pressing sync. The commit message. Shown to everyone.

units._sourceId: The design source this output derives from. The writer must be that source's owner bot - checked against the ring on receipt.
units._version: Per unit, per writer, monotonic. Replace-by-owner-version: a receiver keeps the highest version it has seen for (writerBotCode, unitKey).
units._shape: Inside payload.bin this is the existing sheet package as-is (the *.erks-sheets.json manifest plus its PDFs). Nothing new to parse: the intake that reads a plugin delivery reads this.

The ProjectDesignSource row minus device-local fields (inboxFolder, nativeDocumentPath, local bindings). What another device needs to know the source exists and whose it is - not where it sits on the writer's disk.

_unitKinds: SheetPackage, Quantities, Report, SourceMeta, Visualization. The list is the
'what may travel' contract the ledger asked for first: a unit kind not on it does not
travel, whatever a file is called. Source files (DWG/RVT/MAX) have no kind here and
never will. Project meta and org info are NOT units either - they are the live layer,
_acknowledgements: Appended by receivers as they forward (gossip). The writer sees 'reached M of N'.
An ack is a fact about delivery, not about reading: a device can hold a snapshot it
cannot yet open (no key version yet). Acks are not signed by the writer - they are
signed by each acker, or they are noise.

onReceipt._comment: What a device does with a snapshot, in order. Every refusal is named; nothing is dropped silently.
steps: 3. projectCode must be a project this device is a member of (ring present); else `snapshot_not_a_member` - keep the file in a holding folder, do NOT delete: the ring may arrive later
4. writerBotCode must be in the ring; else `snapshot_writer_not_in_ring`
5. for every unit: the ring must show writerBotCode as the owner of unit.sourceId; else `snapshot_writer_not_source_owner` - the single-writer rule, enforced at the door
6. keyVersion must be one this device holds; else store, mark `snapshot_key_version_unknown`, retry when the ring updates
7. decrypt; verify each unit's contentSha256; refuse `snapshot_payload_hash_mismatch`
8. for each unit: keep if version > held version for (writer, unitKey); else discard as already-held
9. append own ack; forward to other online members (gossip); keep the blob for later carriers
_holdingFolder: Steps 3 and 6 hold rather than refuse. A snapshot that arrives before its ring or
key is the NORMAL case for a device that was off - the carrier path has no ordering.
Holding is bounded (N days, then named as stale), never silent.

_comment: There is no merge. State on a device = for every (writerBotCode, unitKey), the highest
version received. Two writers never own one unit, so two versions of one unit from
different writers cannot exist. This is what the ledger's 'нэгтгэл = бүрдүүлэлт' means:
the project is COMPOSED from single-owner units, not merged.
The one thing a device keeps per peer: 'last snapshot number received from each
writer' - shown in the UI as who is behind whom. The ledger's named residual risk:
a writer's device dies before its latest snapshot reached anyone; that snapshot is
gone. The product shows 'last synced with X: <date>' so the risk is visible, not
removed.

_whatThisDoesNotCover: The live layer (project/org meta) - server-carried, separate contract with SRV.
Album composition (which pages, what order) - live layer by decision; the snapshot
carries pages, the server carries the list. Stated so the seam is not assumed away.
